source_review.notes: Checked current primary documentation for Linux fork, clone, execve, execveat, posix_spawn, the System V ELF loading model, the Linux dynamic loader, auxiliary vectors, capabilities, no-new-privileges, miscellaneous binary formats, proc auxv, and MIT's 2025 xv6 text. All 13 cited URLs returned HTTP 200; platform-specific behaviors are attributed and separated from abstract loader obligations.

evidence: Checked file length F, header offset h, entry count n, entry size q, segment index i, offsets o_i, file sizes f_i, virtual addresses v_i, memory sizes m_i, alignments a_i, page size P, and old/new images O and N for definition before use.
Reviewed process creation, exec, program header, segment, zero-fill, interpreter, auxiliary vector, dynamic loader, relocation, descriptor inheritance, and commit terminology against cited sources.
notation_and_syntax.notes: The notation distinguishes file ranges, virtual-memory ranges, actual page-rounded mappings, image transaction state, and the irreversible commit boundary.

evidence: Executed the two-segment model and confirmed text has 3000 file bytes and 2000 zero bytes, while data has 1200 file bytes and 2896 zero bytes.
Confirmed both offsets are congruent to their virtual addresses modulo 4096, entry 0x400080 lies in executable text, and no segment combines write and execute permissions.
numerical_recomputation.notes: The deterministic calculations establish only the hard-coded plan's basic arithmetic and permission observations.

evidence: Re-derived the subtraction-based header-table bound n times q no greater than F minus h and segment requirements f_i no greater than m_i with nonwrapping file and virtual endpoints.
Checked alignment congruence and page-rounded interval construction, and reviewed the precommit preservation versus postcommit fatal-path transaction argument.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: All algebraic conditions are labeled necessary components of a full format, architecture, policy, mapping, and lifecycle validation.

evidence: Reviewed truncated headers, zero and extreme counts, multiplication and addition wrap, file size exceeding memory size, noncanonical addresses, page-rounded overlap, conflicting permissions, entry outside executable memory, and interpreter recursion.

Reviewed path substitution, mutable files, malicious environment and libraries, inherited descriptors, multithreaded post-fork deadlock, credential transitions, allocation failure, concurrent tracing, and exceptional postcommit failure.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Parser, mapping, ABI, transaction, concurrency, authority, provenance, lifecycle, operational, and safety boundaries receive distinct treatment.

evidence: Traced input, image, authority, sharing, transaction, concurrency, lifecycle, and evidence integrity through exposition, ten examples, and five answers.

evidence: Reviewed the inspect-authorize-plan-allocate-populate-secure-commit-enter argument for both unpublished child creation and existing-image replacement.

Constructed counterexamples for wrapped table bounds, raw nonoverlapping segments whose rounded pages conflict, inherited privileged descriptors, path re-resolution, post-fork locked runtime state, and late rollback claims.
proof_review.notes: The chapter provides reusable validation and transaction obligations, not a formal proof of ELF, Linux exec, a dynamic loader, or deployed launch security.

evidence: Audited uses of valid, safe, atomic, stable, authorize, trusted, secure, successful, exactly once, and certification.
Confirmed ELF specification claims, Linux API semantics, abstract transaction conditions, toy arithmetic, security policy, benchmarks, and human assurance remain differently scoped.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: The commit-point argument explicitly distinguishes recoverable precommit errors from exceptional postcommit termination rather than claiming universal rollback.

Reviewed parser tests, fault injection, creation and relocation timing, cache state, filesystem behavior, provenance, real-time startup, and safety passages for implementation and coverage limitations.
